messages:
Marta: Quick sync — after the slabification rollout we saw a ~12% cost bump for small traces and a few slow tail queries. Root message: noticed extra join/lookup on slab metadata during late enrichment.
Aj: Ugh, that matches the spike graphs I saw. Any easy rollback? :thinking:
Marta: We can revert slab metadata enrichment to inline mode (cheap) or add a deferred async join. Revert would be fastest.
Sam: Before we revert, can we confirm which queries are affected? I grabbed one slow query profile: `SELECT t.*, s.meta FROM traces t JOIN slabs s ON t.slab_id = s.id WHERE t.trace_id = '...'` — the join is causing an extra scatter on hot shards.
Devon: That join is expected now. Slabs shave storage but introduce cross-shard lookups for tiny traces. Tradeoff: smaller cold-storage vs more per-trace IO.
ingest-bot: alert: slab-join-latency > 300ms for 17% of traces in prod (past 10m) :rotating_light:
Marta: Proposed mitigations: 1) short-term revert to pre-slab enrichment (rollback deploy), 2) medium-term: local slab-cache on read path keyed by slab_id, TTL 1m, small memory footprint, 3) long-term: compact slab layout that co-locates metadata for recent traces (slab hotset). Thoughts?
Aj: 1 makes product happy immediately. 2 seems good — how big is the cache? memory math?
Marta: Rough numbers: 1M unique slab_ids/day, hotset ~10k slabs at any time. If each entry is ~120 bytes, cache ~1.2MB * overhead => ~32MB per node. Reasonable.
Sam: Implementation detail: cache must be invalidated on slab rebalance. We should include slab version in key: `slab_id:v` to avoid stale-metadata reads.
Devon: Also watch attribution: billing tags are attached during enrichment. If join is async we risk losing billing context for short-lived spans. That affects cost attribution and chargeback.
Marta: Good catch. For async join we need to attach provisional billing keys at ingest and later patch with slab metadata. That requires write-path idempotency and a reconcile job. More complexity.
Aj: I'd vote revert + cache + planning for co-location. Reconcile cost attribution separately.
Sam: For the revert, runbook: `kubectl set image deploy/ingest ingest=ingest:slab-rollback-20260321` then monitor `ingest-bot` alerts and SLO dashboards.
Devon: One more perf trick: for small traces (<5 spans) we can skip slab lookup entirely and store inline mini-meta to avoid join cost.
Marta: Nice. So final plan: rollback now, roll forward cache + small-trace inline optimization, then iterate on slab co-location design and reconcile billing patch flow. I'll open a short RFC for the co-location step. :thumbsup:
Aj: Sounds good. If Sam can draft the runbook steps I'll trigger the rollback after 10m.
Sam: Drafting runbook now, will post steps + monitors in this thread.
ingest-bot: deploy:ingest status: rollback job queued by Sam at 3612345688
Marta: Thanks — ping here when done and we'll watch the post-rollback latency and cost dashboards.
